docs.title: Lathe
docs.text: Lathe is an open-source terminal AI coding agent powered by dual-model orchestration, local GGUF runtimes, and automated weight merging.

docs.title: Key Highlights
docs.text:
• Dual-Model Orchestration: Pairs a deep reasoning model (e.g. DeepSeek-R1) for planning and code review with a high-throughput code specialist (e.g. Qwen2.5-Coder) for file edits and tool execution.
  • Local First, 100% Private: Runs locally out-of-the-box with Ollama or local inference servers. No code leaves your machine unless you configure remote backends.
  • Automated Model Merging: Interactive mergekit wizard supporting SLERP, TIES, and DARE-TIES. Checks architecture compatibility, quantizes via llama.cpp, creates Ollama Modelfiles, and probes tool-calling accuracy.
  • Defense-in-Depth Safety: Hard regex blocklist for catastrophic commands (rm -rf /, sudo, piped remote scripts), path traversal isolation, secret scrubbing (scrub_env), and instant git checkpoints (/undo).
  • AST Code Indexing & Semantic Search: Tree-sitter AST parsing across Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Go, Rust, and C/C++ with Personalized PageRank symbol ranking and local SQLite vector search.

docs.title: Architecture at a Glance
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    User["Developer Prompt"] --> Router{"Task Router"}
    Router -->|Chat| ReadOnly["Read & Search Tools"]
    Router -->|Simple| Single["Coder Model (Single Mode)"]
    Router -->|Complex| Dual["Dual-Model Orchestrator"]

    subgraph Dual ["Dual-Model Pipeline"]
        Planner["Planner (DeepSeek-R1)"] --> Checklist["Interactive Checklist"]
        Checklist --> Coder["Coder (Qwen2.5-Coder)"]
        Coder --> Reviewer["Reviewer (StepReviewer)"]
        Reviewer -->|Revise| Coder
        Reviewer -->|Approve| Next["Next Step / Done"]
    end

    Single --> Tools["Sandboxed Tools"]
    Coder --> Tools
    Tools --> Checkpoints["Git Checkpoints & Rollback"]

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
# Install with uv tool (recommended)
uv tool install lathe-agent

# Run environment and model health check
lathe doctor

# Start interactive agent session
lathe

docs.title: Choosing Models
docs.text: Lathe divides agent execution across four specialized roles: Coder, Planner, Reviewer, and Router. Selecting appropriate models for your hardware configuration optimizes latency, throughput, and accuracy.

docs.title: Role Responsibilities
docs.text: Role Responsibility Ideal Model Characteristics Recommended Local Model Coder Inspects files, produces targeted unified diffs, runs test suites, executes shell tools. Strong syntax adherence, high coding benchmark score, reliable function calling. qwen2.5-coder:7b or qwen2.5-coder:1.5b Planner Deconstructs complex tasks, synthesizes repository maps, writes structured JSON execution steps. Deep chain-of-thought reasoning, strong architectural planning. deepseek-r1:8b or deepseek-r1:7b Reviewer Evaluates coder step diffs and test results against Lathe's review rubric. Critical code audit skills, bug detection, schema validation. Defaults to Planner (deepseek-r1:8b) Router Classifies incoming developer messages into chat, simple, or complex, writes compaction summaries. Lightweight, high throughput, low latency. qwen2.5-coder:1.5b or qwen2.5:1.5b

docs.title: Tier 1: Laptop (8 GB - 16 GB Unified Memory / RAM)
docs.text:
• Coder: qwen2.5-coder:1.5b (Q4_K_M ~1.0 GB RAM)
  • Planner: deepseek-r1:1.5b or qwen2.5-coder:7b
  • Router: qwen2.5-coder:1.5b
ollama pull qwen2.5-coder:1.5b
ollama pull deepseek-r1:1.5b

docs.title: Tier 2: Workstation (16 GB - 32 GB RAM or VRAM)
docs.text:
• Coder: qwen2.5-coder:7b (Q4_K_M ~4.7 GB RAM)
  • Planner: deepseek-r1:8b (Q4_K_M ~4.9 GB RAM)
  • Router: qwen2.5-coder:1.5b
ollama pull qwen2.5-coder:7b
ollama pull deepseek-r1:8b
ollama pull qwen2.5-coder:1.5b

docs.title: Tier 3: High-End Workstation (32 GB - 64 GB+ RAM or VRAM)
docs.text:
• Coder: qwen2.5-coder:14b or qwen2.5-coder:32b
  • Planner: deepseek-r1:14b or deepseek-r1:32b
  • Router: qwen2.5-coder:7b

docs.title: Calibrating Tool Calling with lathe models probe
docs.text:
Different GGUF quantizations handle tool calling via either native function calling or fallback <tool_call> parsing. Run the automatic probe utility to test your model's capabilities:

lathe models probe qwen2.5-coder:7b

Lathe will run a sample tool call against the model, determine whether native or fallback schema parsing performs reliably, and cache the preferred protocol in .lathe/models_cache.json.

docs.title: Configuration Reference
docs.text:
Lathe reads configuration from two files: 1. Global Configuration: ~/.config/lathe/lathe.toml (applies across all projects) 2. Project Configuration: ./lathe.toml in your project root (overrides global settings)

To generate a starter configuration file in your project, run: 

lathe config init

docs.title: Full lathe.toml Specification
docs.text:
[project]
# Custom test command override (auto-detected if omitted)
test_command = "pytest"

[settings]
# Operating mode: "auto" (intelligent router), "single" (coder only), or "dual" (planner + coder)
mode = "auto"

# Permission mode: "default" (interactive prompts), "auto", or "yolo"
permission_mode = "default"

# Maximum agent steps before halting execution
max_agent_steps = 25

# Token budget allocated to repository symbol map
repomap_token_budget = 2048

# Enable automated post-run test execution and self-correction in single mode
self_check = true

# ==============================================================================
# Model Roles
# Supported backends: "ollama", "huggingface", "openai-compatible"
# ==============================================================================

[roles.coder]
backend = "ollama"
model = "qwen2.5-coder:7b"
temperature = 0.0
max_tokens = 4096
context_window = 32768
base_url = "http://localhost:11434"

[roles.planner]
backend = "ollama"
model = "deepseek-r1:8b"
temperature = 0.0
max_tokens = 4096
context_window = 16384
base_url = "http://localhost:11434"

[roles.reviewer]
backend = "ollama"
model = "deepseek-r1:8b"
temperature = 0.0
max_tokens = 2048
context_window = 16384
base_url = "http://localhost:11434"

[roles.router]
backend = "ollama"
model = "qwen2.5-coder:1.5b"
temperature = 0.0
max_tokens = 1024
context_window = 8192
base_url = "http://localhost:11434"

# ==============================================================================
# Semantic Code Search & Embeddings
# ==============================================================================

[embeddings]
# Provider: "ollama", "sentence-transformers", or "huggingface"
provider = "ollama"
model = "nomic-embed-text"
base_url = "http://localhost:11434"

# ==============================================================================
# Model Context Protocol (MCP) Client Integrations
# ==============================================================================

[mcp.servers.github]
command = "npx"
args = ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-github"]
env = { GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN = "env:GITHUB_TOKEN" }

[mcp.servers.filesystem]
command = "npx"
args = ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem", "./docs"]

docs.title: Project Instructions (LATHE.md)
docs.text:
Create a LATHE.md file in your repository root (or globally at ~/.config/lathe/LATHE.md) to define stack conventions, testing guidelines, and architectural rules. Lathe automatically loads LATHE.md into the agent's system prompt and planning context.

Run /init inside Lathe to have the agent explore the repository and draft a baseline LATHE.md.

docs.title: Custom Slash Commands (.lathe/commands/<name>.md)
docs.text:
Create markdown templates in .lathe/commands/<name>.md to define project-specific workflows accessible via /<name>.

Example .lathe/commands/fix-issue.md: 

Read issue description: $ARGS
Inspect the relevant source files and tests, write a reproduction test, implement the fix, and verify tests pass.
Invoked in the terminal via /fix-issue 42.

docs.title: Contributing to Lathe
docs.text: Thank you for your interest in contributing to Lathe! We welcome bug fixes, documentation improvements, new tools, and architectural enhancements.

docs.title: Development Setup
docs.text: Lathe requires Python 3.11+ and uses Astral uv for fast, reproducible virtual environments.

docs.title: 1. Clone the Repository
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/adityasurse/lathe.git
cd lathe

docs.title: 2. Set Up Virtual Environment with uv
docs.text:
# Create virtual environment and install development dependencies
uv venv
source .venv/bin/activate  # On Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
uv pip install -e ".[dev,merge]"

docs.title: 3. Verify Local Installation
docs.text: lathe doctor

docs.title: Code Quality Standards
docs.text: Before submitting a pull request, ensure all linters, formatters, type checks, and tests pass with zero errors:

docs.title: Linting & Formatting (Ruff)
docs.text:
# Check code style
uv run ruff check .

# Check formatting
uv run ruff format --check .

# Auto-format
uv run ruff format .

docs.title: Strict Type Checking (Mypy)
docs.text: uv run mypy src

docs.title: Test Suite Execution (Pytest)
docs.text:
# Run standard test suite
uv run pytest

# Run with coverage report
uv run pytest --cov=src/lathe/tools --cov=src/lathe/safety --cov=src/lathe/orchestrator --cov=src/lathe/context --cov-report=term

docs.title: Phase-Style Pull Requests
docs.text: Lathe follows a structured, milestone-driven phase development methodology. When opening a PR: 1. Self-Contained Focus: Keep pull requests focused on a single logical feature, tool, or bug fix. 2. Comprehensive Unit Tests: Accompany every new tool or orchestrator capability with targeted unit tests achieving 80%+ branch/statement coverage. 3. No Breaking Safety Boundaries: Never weaken PermissionEngine blocklists or path confinement. 4. Update Documentation: Update corresponding documentation in docs/ and architectural notes in ARCHITECTURE.md.

docs.title: Issue Labels
docs.text: Look for issues tagged with: - good first issue: Ideal for newcomers to get familiar with Lathe's codebase. - help wanted: Architectural features or tools actively seeking community implementation. - bug: Confirmed bugs or test regressions. - documentation: Guides, tutorials, and doc improvements.

docs.title: Dual-LLM Mode
docs.text: Dual-model orchestration pairs an expert software architect (Planner) with a disciplined execution specialist (Coder) to tackle complex multi-file refactoring and feature additions.

docs.title: Execution Flow
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor User as Developer
    participant Dual as DualAgent Orchestrator
    participant Planner as Planner Model (DeepSeek-R1)
    participant Coder as Coder Model (Qwen2.5-Coder)
    participant Reviewer as StepReviewer
    participant Tools as Tool Execution

    User->>Dual: Submit complex task
    Dual->>Planner: Task + Repo Map + Search Results
    Planner-->>Dual: JSON Plan {goal, steps, risks}
    Dual->>User: Display Interactive Plan Checklist
    User->>Dual: Approve [y] / Edit [e]
    loop For each step in plan
        Dual->>Coder: Step instructions + Focused file context
        Coder->>Tools: Edit files, run test suite
        Tools-->>Coder: Tool outcomes
        Coder-->>Dual: Step completed
        Dual->>Reviewer: Step diff + test results
        alt Verdict is Approve
            Reviewer-->>Dual: Approve
            Dual->>Planner: Step summary
            Planner-->>Dual: Optional plan revision
        else Verdict is Revise
            Reviewer-->>Dual: Revise (file, problem, suggestion)
            Dual->>Coder: Retry step with feedback (up to 2 retries)
        end
    end
    Dual-->>User: Final Report

docs.title: 1. Structured Plan Generation
docs.text:
The planner model receives: 1. High-level task prompt 2. Project conventions from LATHE.md 3. Repository symbol map ranked by Personalized PageRank 4. Keyword and vector code search results

It produces a validated JSON execution plan conforming to Lathe's Pydantic schema:

{
  "goal": "Add JWT authentication middleware and unit tests",
  "steps": [
    {
      "id": 1,
      "title": "Create auth configuration",
      "files_to_read": ["src/config.py"],
      "files_to_change": ["src/auth_config.py"],
      "instructions": "Implement AuthConfig loading JWT secret from environment",
      "done_when": "Unit tests pass"
    },
    {
      "id": 2,
      "title": "Add token validation middleware",
      "files_to_read": ["src/auth_config.py"],
      "files_to_change": ["src/middleware.py"],
      "instructions": "Extract Bearer tokens from Authorization headers",
      "done_when": "Integration test succeeds"
    }
  ],
  "risks": [
    "Token expiration edge case handling in expired sessions"
  ]
}

If the model produces malformed JSON, Lathe automatically feeds the validation error back for an immediate single-shot correction.

docs.title: 2. Interactive Checklist & User Approval
docs.text:
Before any code is altered, Lathe presents the plan in an interactive Rich terminal checklist:

  • [y]es: Approve plan as written and begin automated step execution.
  • [e]dit: Opens your $EDITOR (e.g. nano, vim, or code) on the raw plan JSON. Changes are validated upon save.
  • [n]o: Reject the plan and return to prompt without modifying any files.

docs.title: 3. Focused Coder Execution
docs.text: Unlike naive agents that dump entire conversation histories into context, Lathe runs the coder on a focused context window for each step: - Only the active step's instructions and verification criteria (done_when) - Pinned target files (@file) - Repository symbol map - Concise summaries of completed earlier steps

docs.title: 4. Step Review Rubric
docs.text:
After a step completes, the StepReviewer audits the unified git diff and test output against Lathe's five-point rubric: 1. Correctness: Does the code achieve the step objective without regressions? 2. Step Match: Does the change strictly implement the agreed step instructions? 3. No Unrelated Changes: Are modifications confined strictly to target files? 4. No Secrets: Are API keys, passwords, or tokens hardcoded? 5. Tests Pass: Did the automated test suite finish with zero failures?

If the review verdict is revise, the coder retries with specific line-by-line feedback. If retries exceed 2, the user is prompted to [k]eep, [u]ndo this step, or [t]ake over.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: This guide walks you through installing Lathe, verifying your local environment, and launching your first agent coding session.

docs.title: Option 1: Astral uv Tool (Recommended)
docs.text:
Astral uv provides isolated, high-speed Python tool execution:

uv tool install lathe-agent

To include model merging with mergekit: 

uv tool install "lathe-agent[merge]"

docs.title: Option 2: pipx
docs.text: pipx install lathe-agent

docs.title: Option 3: Quick Install One-Liners
docs.text:
Linux / macOS: 

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/adityasurse/lathe/main/install.sh | bash

Windows PowerShell: 

irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/adityasurse/lathe/main/install.ps1 | iex

docs.title: Environment Health Check
docs.text:
Before your first session, verify that your local runtime (such as Ollama) and tools are properly detected:

lathe doctor

Output checks: - Python environment version ($\ge 3.11$) - Git binary and repository root detection - Ripgrep (rg) availability (falls back to Python search if absent) - Ollama service reachability and installed models - Hugging Face token verification (masked for security)

docs.title: Interactive REPL Mode
docs.text:
Launch the full-featured interactive terminal session in your project root:

cd /path/to/your/project
lathe

docs.title: REPL Features:
docs.text:
• @file autocompletion: Type @ followed by filename characters to search repository paths.
  • Multiline Editing: Press Alt+Enter (or Esc+Enter) to insert newlines without submitting.
  • Cancel Turn: Press Ctrl+C to cancel a streaming completion or halt a tool.
  • Clean Exit: Type /exit or press Ctrl+D.

docs.title: Built-in Slash Commands:
docs.text: Command Description /help Display interactive command guide /mode [single\|dual\|auto] Switch agent orchestrator mode /model [role] [name] Switch model assigned to role (coder, planner, router) /tokens Display colored breakdown chart of context budget /compact Force compaction of older conversation turns /diff Display working tree unified diff since session start /checkpoints List checkpoint snapshot history /undo Roll back recent agent edits to previous checkpoint /clear Clear conversation history /stats View telemetry table (tokens/sec, latency, call counts)

docs.title: Headless CLI Execution
docs.text:
Execute specific tasks directly from your shell without opening the interactive prompt:

# Autonomous single-shot execution
lathe "Add input validation to src/auth.py and run pytest"

# Explicit dual-model execution
lathe --dual "Refactor the database connection pool across all services"

# Non-interactive automated execution (bypasses permission prompts)
lathe --auto "Fix typos in README.md"

docs.title: Hugging Face Setup
docs.text: Lathe integrates natively with Hugging Face for remote inference, token downloads, architecture compatibility checks, and publishing merged models.

docs.title: Setting Up Your Hugging Face Token
docs.text: Lathe strictly isolates API secrets to environment variables to ensure tokens are never saved to project files or leaked in git commits.

docs.title: Step 1: Obtain an Access Token
docs.text:
1. Go to Hugging Face Settings > Tokens.
  2. Create a token:
  3. Read token: Sufficient for architecture compatibility checks and remote inference.
  4. Write token: Required if pushing merged weights via lathe merge push <name>.

docs.title: Step 2: Set the Token in Your Environment
docs.text:
macOS / Linux: 

export HF_TOKEN="hf_your_secret_token_here"

To persist across terminal sessions, add the export to your shell configuration (~/.zshrc or ~/.bashrc).

Windows PowerShell: 

$env:HF_TOKEN = "hf_your_secret_token_here"

docs.title: Hugging Face Inference Providers API
docs.text:
You can configure any role (coder, planner, or router) to utilize cloud models via Hugging Face's serverless Inference Providers API in lathe.toml:

[roles.coder]
backend = "huggingface"
model = "Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct"
temperature = 0.0
max_tokens = 4096
context_window = 32768

Supported serverless providers are queried automatically based on latency and availability.

docs.title: Model Architecture Pre-Checks
docs.text:
When performing model merges with lathe merge, Lathe communicates with the Hugging Face Hub using huggingface_hub to fetch and validate model specifications without downloading multi-gigabyte weight tensors.

It verifies: - model_type compatibility (e.g. qwen2 matching qwen2) - hidden_size matching across both models - num_hidden_layers alignment - vocab_size and tokenizer compatibility

Pairs with mismatched architectures are refused before downloading weights.

docs.title: Publishing Merged Weights
docs.text:
Once a model is merged into merges/<name>, you can upload it directly to your Hugging Face account:

lathe merge push my-merged-coder

By default, repositories are created with private visibility unless you explicitly confirm public release.

docs.title: Model Merging
docs.text: Lathe includes a complete model combination and conversion pipeline powered by mergekit and llama.cpp. It allows developers to create custom hybrid models (e.g. combining a code specialist with an instruction-following model) and run them locally.

docs.title: The lathe merge Wizard
docs.text:
Launch the interactive wizard:

lathe merge

docs.title: 1. Selecting Candidate Models
docs.text:
Choose two Hugging Face safetensors repositories. You can pick popular presets or specify custom repository IDs: - Preset (Laptops): Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B + Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct - Custom (Workstations): Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-7B + deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B

(Note: Hugging Face safetensors repos are required; GGUF repositories cannot be merged directly).

docs.title: 2. Architecture Compatibility Pre-Check
docs.text:
Before downloading weights (saving gigabytes of bandwidth and disk space), Lathe queries the Hugging Face Hub using huggingface_hub to verify architecture compatibility: - model_type (must match, e.g. qwen2) - hidden_size - num_hidden_layers - vocab_size and tokenizer configuration

If architectures diverge, Lathe displays a formatted table highlighting differences and halts safely.

docs.title: 3. Choosing Merge Method
docs.text:
• SLERP (Spherical Linear Interpolation): Recommended for combining two fine-tuned models derived from the same base. Supports interpolation parameter $t \in [0, 1]$ and per-layer gradients.
  • TIES (Trim, Elect Sign & Merge): Resolves parameter interference by trimming small magnitude deltas and electing unanimous parameter signs.
  • DARE-TIES: Drop And REscale variant of TIES preserving base model generalization.
  • Linear: Simple weighted arithmetic average of model weights.

docs.title: 4. Hardware Estimation
docs.text: Lathe calculates parameters and required memory ($\text{params} \times 2 \text{ bytes}$ for FP16), inspects available RAM and disk space, and warns if resources are constrained.

docs.title: Running Locally
docs.text:
Lathe generates the configuration into merges/<name>/config.yaml and executes mergekit-yaml using lazy unpickling and low-memory CPU options:

lathe merge --name my-custom-merge

docs.title: Running in Google Colab (--colab)
docs.text:
If your local machine lacks sufficient RAM or GPU compute, pass --colab to generate a self-contained Google Colab notebook (.ipynb):

lathe merge --colab --name my-colab-merge

The notebook configures GPU runtime, installs mergekit, executes the merge, and uploads results directly to your Hugging Face Hub account.

docs.title: GGUF Quantization & Ollama Deployment
docs.text:
Once your model is merged into merges/<name>, convert and quantize it for instant local inference in Ollama:

lathe merge gguf my-custom-merge --quant Q4_K_M

This automated step: 1. Clones and compiles llama.cpp in ~/.cache/lathe/llama.cpp (pinned to a stable release). 2. Converts safetensors to FP16 GGUF using convert_hf_to_gguf.py. 3. Quantizes weights using llama-quantize to your target format (default Q4_K_M). 4. Generates an Ollama Modelfile preserving the parent model's exact Jinja chat template. 5. Runs ollama create lathe-my-custom-merge -f Modelfile. 6. Calibrates tool calling with lathe models probe lathe-my-custom-merge.

docs.title: Safety & Security
docs.text: Autonomous coding agents require robust safety boundaries. Lathe implements a multi-tiered security architecture designed to prevent accidental data loss, shell command abuse, path traversal, credential leakage, and prompt injection attacks.

docs.title: Threat Model Overview
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    subgraph Inputs ["Untrusted Inputs"]
        Code["Repository Files & Prompts"]
        Pipes["Remote Script Executables"]
    end

    subgraph Gates ["Lathe Safety Gates"]
        Delimiter["1. Delimiter Wrapping<br/>([UNTRUSTED CONTENT])"]
        Confinement["2. Workspace Path Confinement<br/>(PathEscapeError)"]
        Blocklist["3. Hard Security Blocklist<br/>(Unconditional Rejection)"]
        Scrubbing["4. Secret Scrubbing<br/>(scrub_env)"]
        Checkpoints["5. Git Commit Snapshots<br/>(Non-destructive Rollback)"]
    end

    subgraph OS ["Operating System"]
        Proc["Process Group Execution (os.setsid)"]
    end

    Inputs --> Delimiter
    Delimiter --> Confinement
    Confinement --> Blocklist
    Blocklist --> Scrubbing
    Scrubbing --> Checkpoints
    Checkpoints --> Proc

docs.title: 1. Hard Security Blocklist
docs.text:
Regardless of operational mode (even when running with --auto or --yolo), Lathe strictly rejects catastrophic command patterns:

  • Root & Home Deletion: rm -rf /, rm -rf ~, rm -rf $HOME
  • Privilege Escalation: sudo, su, doas
  • Remote Code Pipelines: curl ... | sh, wget ... | bash, fetch ... | zsh
  • Disk Wiping: mkfs, raw device dd targeting /dev/*
  • Dangerous Git Actions: git push --force, git clean -fdx
  • System Tampering: chmod -R 777 /, fork bombs (:(){ :|:& };:)

Blocklist violations trigger immediate rejection with structured feedback to the model.

docs.title: 2. Permission Engine Modes
docs.text: Configure authorization behavior via --mode or lathe.toml:

docs.title: default (Interactive)
docs.text:
• Read tools (read_file, list_dir, glob, grep_search, semantic_search) run automatically.
  • Mutating tools (write_file, edit_file, run_shell, git_commit) prompt the developer before execution:
  • [y]es: Allow this specific invocation once.
  • [n]o: Reject this tool call with feedback to the model.
  • [a]lways: Whitelist this command pattern for the rest of the project in .lathe/permissions.json.
  • [e]dit: Modify the shell command or file arguments interactively before running.
  • [d]eny with message: Provide explicit instructions explaining why the tool was rejected.

docs.title: auto (Autonomous)
docs.text: Permits standard file edits and project test commands automatically while still actively enforcing the hard blocklist and workspace path boundaries.

docs.title: yolo (Unattended)
docs.text: Runs non-interactively without prompting, while maintaining unconditional blocklist defenses.

docs.title: 3. Workspace Path Confinement
docs.text: All file paths are resolved through Workspace.resolve_path(). Attempts to read or modify files outside the configured workspace root (e.g. ../../etc/passwd or external symlinks) immediately raise PathEscapeError and halt the agent.

docs.title: 4. Secret Sanitization (scrub_env)
docs.text: Subprocesses spawned by Lathe (run_shell, run_tests, git operations) execute in an isolated environment sanitized by scrub_env(). Any environment variable matching sensitive patterns (*_KEY, *_SECRET, *_TOKEN, AWS_*, GITHUB_*, HF_*) is stripped to prevent credential exfiltration.

docs.title: 5. Git Checkpoints & Non-Destructive Undo
docs.text:
Before executing any mutating file edit or shell tool, Lathe captures a git commit snapshot in an isolated reference (refs/lathe/checkpoints/<session>/<n>) using git write-tree without modifying your branch, staging area, or git reflog:

  • /diff: View exact changes made by the agent since session inception.
  • /undo or lathe undo: Instantly revert the workspace to the state prior to the agent's recent step.
  • /checkpoints: View snapshot history with timestamps and descriptions.
